title: Mao's 30 June 1949 speech calls the coming order a people's democratic dictatorship
summary: On 30 June 1949 Mao described the coming government as a people's democratic dictatorship.
body: Fordham prints Mao's 30 June 1949 speech, given for the twenty-eighth anniversary of the Chinese Communist Party, under the title On the People's Democratic Dictatorship. The name of the order is his. The speech is a program on the eve of the People's Republic, not a constitution. The wording on the page includes: "of the working class, and advance from this to the establishment of a state which is a people's democratic dictatorship under the leadership of the working class and based on the alliance of workers and peasants. Externally, unite in a common struggle with those nations of the world which treat us as equals and unite with the peoples of all countries. That is, ally ourselves". The evidence label is the truth-gate ceiling for this host. The host is not on the gate's primary-text or official list, so the label is weak. The quotation is still the page's wording.
